seo_title: Delhi HC Upholds Arbitral Award Against DDA Appeal
title: Delhi High Court Dismisses DDA's Appeal, Holds Reappraisal of Evidence Impermissible Under Section 37 Arbitration Act
case_name: Delhi Development Authority v. S.K. Singla & Anr.
citation: FAO(OS)(COMM) 292/2026; Division Bench judgment dated 3 November 2026 (Kshetarpal and Parashar, JJ.)
card_summary: A Division Bench dismissed DDA's appeal against an arbitral award favouring a residential plot purchaser. DDA argued its files were untraceable, but the court held this did not show adequate efforts to retrieve the specific records during arbitration, and a later building-plan sanction did not prove earlier compliance. The bench reaffirmed that Section 37 bars reappraisal of evidence the arbitrator already weighed.
card_tip: An appellant under Section 37 cannot reopen factual findings an arbitrator already weighed on the material before it; producing better evidence later, or arguing records went missing, will not unsettle the award.
verification_notes: The appeal number FAO(OS)(COMM) 292/2026, the Division Bench (Kshetarpal and Parashar, JJ.) and the pronouncement date of 3 November 2026 are confirmed by the Delhi High Court's own judgment-portal filing (filename encodes 03112026) and corroborated by the TaxGuru and CourtKutchehry case reports naming the same parties and appeal number. The reasoning on the untraceable-files argument and the later building-plan sanction comes from the TaxGuru summary; the underlying arbitral award amount and the plot particulars were not independently confirmed from the full judgment text, so the card does not state them.
